findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the REBAR_DETECTED_BY env read happens in the shared `create_core` seam (covering CLI, python-library, and MCP ingresses), with the optional `--detected-by` flag layered at the CLI as an explicit override.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:79-126: `create_ticket` calls `composer.create_core(...)` directly (python ingress), not the CLI
src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:211 `create_cli` is only the CLI route; `create_core` (line 73) is the shared seam all ingresses converge on
Plan Approach: "'rebar create' reads and stamps" and "--detected-by flag overrides env" frames the read in CLI-parsing context
findings.finding: The plan targets AUTOMATED filers (canary/CI/review-bot) but locates the env-var read at the CLI command module ('src/rebar/_commands/create.py (or the create command module)') with CLI-flag precedence, whereas library (`_lib_writes.create_ticket`) and MCP (`_mcp_writes.create_ticket`) ingresses converge on `create_core` WITHOUT going through the CLI arg parser — so an env read placed only in `create_cli` would fail to stamp REBAR_DETECTED_BY for python/MCP-based automated filers.
scenarios: A review-bot files bugs via the MCP `create_ticket` tool with REBAR_DETECTED_BY=review-bot set; if the env read lives in `create_cli`, the field is never stamped
A CI job files via the python library `rebar.create_ticket`; same miss
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Scope bullet to place the env-var read in `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:create_core` (the seam every ingress converges on), passing an explicit `detected_by` param down from `create_cli`/`create_ticket`/MCP so the CLI flag can override the env-derived default without excluding non-CLI filers.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the new `detected_by` create-event field with the EXISTING production `detected_by:<source>` tag namespace (reads.py:370-372, cli-reference.md:290, test_has_tag_detected_by.py): either justify why an env/creation-time first-class field is needed over (or alongside) the tag mechanism, and state how the metrics lens unifies both, OR extend the existing tag namespace instead of adding a parallel field.
evidence: Existing tag namespace query logic: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:370-372 — `if has_tag.startswith("detected_by:") and not ticket_type: ticket_type = "bug"` (bug-only auto-intersect)
Test-pinned: tests/interfaces/queries/test_has_tag_detected_by.py seeds `rebar.tag(bug, "detected_by:tests")` and pins `--has-tag=detected_by:tests` returns only bugs
Documented: docs/cli-reference.md:290 and src/rebar/_cli/help/list.txt:9 — 'tags matching ^detected_by: auto-intersect with --type=bug'
The plan's Approach/Scope reference no existing mechanism; it treats `detected_by` as brand-new (env var, flag, schema field, metrics lens)
FP7 check: the existing mechanism lives in src/ + docs/ + pinned tests (production), NOT under docs/experiments/ or a *_poc.* path — so the designated-experiment carve-out does not apply
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new first-class `detected_by` create-event field (plus REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var, --detected-by flag, compiled-state schema field, and a metrics lens) to record a bug's detection channel, but the codebase ALREADY has a production `detected_by:<source>` TAG namespace serving the same 'which channel found this bug' purpose — bug-only (auto-intersects with --type=bug), queryable via --has-tag=detected_by:*, documented, and test-pinned. The plan never acknowledges or reconciles with this existing mechanism, risking two parallel `detected_by` concepts with divergent query surfaces.
findings.location: Approach / Scope / AC1 (whole plan — the `detected_by` field design)
scenarios: A user tags a bug `detected_by:canary` (existing path) AND another bug is created with REBAR_DETECTED_BY=canary (new field) — the two are stored/queried differently, so escape-channel trend queries silently miss one population
A maintainer greps `detected_by` and finds two unrelated implementations with the same name and overlapping intent
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit 'Relationship to the existing detected_by: tag namespace' subsection to the Approach. If the new field is retained, state the distinction (env-driven, creation-time, project-scoped vs. human post-hoc bug-only tags) and specify whether the metrics lens reads BOTH sources so trend queries are complete; otherwise fold detection-channel capture into the existing tag mechanism (e.g. stamp a `detected_by:<value>` tag from REBAR_DETECTED_BY at create) rather than adding a parallel state field.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Evaluate reusing the existing `detected_by:<source>` tag namespace (stamp a `detected_by:<value>` tag at create via the existing `tags` path) versus adding a new parallel scalar field, and justify the chosen path — reconciling the name collision and single-source-of-truth for escape-channel metrics.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:370-372: `if has_tag.startswith("detected_by:") and not ticket_type: ticket_type = "bug"` — established bug-only queryable tag namespace
docs/cli-reference.md:290: `tags matching ^detected_by: auto-intersect with --type=bug` — already documented
tests/interfaces/queries/test_has_tag_detected_by.py:26-32 seeds `bug[detected_by:tests]` and pins the bug-only filter semantics

src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:158-162 / _lib_writes.py:87: `create_core`/`create_ticket` already accept a `tags` list at creation — an env-var/flag could stamp a `detected_by:<value>` tag with NO schema/reducer/registry change
Plan Approach proposes a new event field + schema + reducer projection + registry entry with no mention of the existing tag mechanism
findings.finding: The repo already has a production `detected_by:<source>` TAG namespace (bug-only, queryable via `--has-tag=detected_by:*`, documented, test-pinned) that records the same concept the plan proposes as a NEW scalar `detected_by` event field; the plan never acknowledges or compares against it, creating two competing sources of truth and a literal name collision (field `detected_by` vs tag prefix `detected_by:`).
scenarios: A client already querying `--has-tag=detected_by:canary` now has escape-channel data split across a tag (old bugs) and a scalar field (new bugs) that can disagree
An agent reads 'detected_by' and cannot tell whether to set the tag or the new field; a metrics query built on one surface silently misses data recorded on the other
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Approach paragraph that names the existing `detected_by:` tag namespace and states a positive rationale for a scalar field over a tag (e.g. env-driven, non-user-visible provenance vs. a user-facing filterable tag), OR pivot to stamping a `detected_by:` tag through the existing `tags` create path to avoid schema/reducer/registry changes and the two-sources-of-truth problem.

findings.finding: The plan characterizes the reducer work as merely 'reducer-tolerated' / additive (AC3: 'existing stores/reducers tolerate events without it') implying NO reducer change is needed, but this premise is refuted by the CREATE reducer: it whitelists each key it projects into compiled state and does not copy unknown event-data fields. Since 'rebar show' returns compiled reducer state (not the raw event), a detected_by field stamped only on the CREATE event will NOT appear in 'rebar show' unless the reducer is given an explicit present-only projection block — directly contradicting the plan's own Testing/AC1 requirement that the field is 'shown by rebar show'.
findings.location: Scope ('event schema: optional detected_by field ... additive, reducer-tolerated'); Testing ('field present in event and shown by rebar show'); AC1 & AC3
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, change the event-schema line to require a reducer projection: 'process_create surfaces detected_by additively (present-only), mirroring the existing source_*/creation_channel projection blocks, so it appears in compiled state / rebar show while an event without it reduces byte-identically.'

findings.finding: The plan's Scope names 'event schema: optional detected_by field on create events (additive, reducer-tolerated)' but does not enumerate the two concrete consumer edits OUTSIDE the create command dir that the established source_*/creation_channel precedent proves are required: (a) an explicit copy of the field into compiled state in the reducer's process_create, and (b) a declaration of the field in the compiled-state schema.
findings.location: Scope — 'event schema: optional detected_by field on create events (additive, reducer-tolerated)'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Scope: 'src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py: process_create copies detected_by into compiled state (mirroring source_*)' and 'src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json: declare the optional detected_by string field'.
